newsitem.title: USA: U.S. denies bail for accused spy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. denies bail for accused spy.

text.p: A federal judge on Monday denied bail for FBI agent Earl Pitts, who was charged last week with being a spy for the Soviet Union and Russia
"There is substantial reason to believe the defendant would want to flee if released," U.S. Judge Rawles Jones said in denying a motion by Pitts' attorney that he be released on bail.
Pitts, who has been an FBI agent for 13 years, was arrested last Wednesday and charged with spying for the Soviet KGB and its Russian successor intelligence agency.

FBI Agent David Lambert testified at the bail hearing that an escape plan was found in a computer in Pitts' office in 1995 when the FBI had him under surveillance. The judge said there would be a threat to national security if Pitts was released.
"Mr. Pitts will be held without condition of release," the judge said.
Pitts, 43, was scheduled to be arraigned next week. No trial date has been set.
